sentences.text:
The present writ petition has been filed for issuance of direction upon the concerned respondents to provide adequate land/rehabilitate the petitioners in lieu of acquisition of their agricultural land appertaining to Plot Nos. 18, 21 & 22, Khata No. 04,
Village-Kusumbad, Thana No. 568, Mohanpur Circle, District- Deoghar, as the same was the only source of their livelihood.
In alternative, the petitioners have prayed for enhancement of compensation in lieu of acquisition of the aforesaid land.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that though the petitioners' aforesaid land has been acquired by the State authorities for construction of Chandan Canal under Punasi Dam Project,
Deoghar, however, they have not been rehabilitated as the said agricultural land was the only source of their livelihood.
Moreover, the petitioners have also not been paid appropriate compensation.

3. Mr. Om Prakash Tiwari, learned GP-III appearing on behalf of the respondents, submits that rehabilitation of land losers is dependent upon the applicable Rehabilitation and Resettlement Policy of the Government.
However, the petitioners have not brought on record any such policy in support of the said claim.

So far as the issue with respect to payment of compensation in lieu of acquisition of the said land is concerned, an award was already prepared in the name of the petitioner no. 1 and the husband of the petitioner no. 2 for an amount of Rs.20,59,739/-.

If the petitioners were not satisfied with the said quantum of compensation, they should have taken Gopal Naraune vs The State Of Jharkhand on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43333807/

Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Having heard learned counsel for the parties and considering that the petitioners have neither averred about nor have brought on record any such policy of the Government with respect to rehabilitation of the land losers under the said project, no writ of mandamus on that aspect can be issued at present.

Moreover, so far as the petitioners' contention that compensation for acquisition of the said land fixed by the competent authority i.e., the respondent no. 3 - the District Land Acquisition Officer, Deoghar is not adequate, they have the liberty to take recourse of Section 64 of the Act, 2013.

5. Accordingly, the petitioners are given liberty to prefer an application before the respondent no. 3 for referring the matter to the Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority-cum- Principal District Judge, Deoghar in terms with Section 64 of the Act, 2013 for determination of fair compensation.
On receipt of the said application, the respondent no. 3 shall refer the matter within 30 days to the said Authority under the Act, 2013 for determination.
6. The writ petition is accordingly disposed of with aforesaid liberty and direction.
(Rajesh Shankar, J.) Manish Gopal Naraune vs The State Of Jharkhand on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43333807/
